blocks.text: Proteins are large, complex macromolecules found abundantly in all living organisms: skin, hair, haemoglobin (the red pigment of blood) and muscles are all proteins. They have key roles in the body, from building tissues to the many functions of cells and organs, and any change in the structure or function of a protein can make the body behave abnormally. When proteins are completely hydrolysed they give amino acids; about 20 different amino acids link together in various sequences to make the great variety of proteins.

blocks.prompt: What do proteins give on complete hydrolysis?

items: Proteins: large molecules of amino acids (about 20 kinds) found in all living things.
